chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿImrān asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said:

For what reason is the recitation done aloud in Ṣalāt al-Jumuʿah, Ṣalāt al-Maghrib, Ṣalāt al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah, and Ṣalāt al-Ghadāh, while in the other prayers, al-Ẓuhr and al-ʿAṣr, it is not recited aloud? And for what reason did tasbīḥ in the last two rakʿahs become better than recitation?

He said: “Because when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was taken by night to the heaven, the first prayer Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordained upon him was al-Ẓuhr on the day of al-Jumuʿah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, added the angels to him, praying behind him, and He commanded His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله to recite aloud so that He might make his excellence clear to them. Then Allah ordained al-ʿAṣr upon him and did not add to him anyone from the angels, and He commanded him to recite quietly because there was no one behind him. Then He ordained al-Maghrib upon him and added the angels to him and commanded him to recite aloud, and likewise al-ʿIshāʾ al-Ākhirah. Then when it was near al-Fajr, he descended, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ordained al-Fajr upon him and commanded him to recite aloud so that He might make its excellence clear to the people just as He had made it clear to the angels. For this reason recitation is done aloud in them. And tasbīḥ became better than recitation in the last two rakʿahs because when the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله was in the last two, he remembered what he had seen of the greatness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and was struck with awe, so he said:
“Subḥāna Allāh, wa al-ḥamdu lillāh, wa lā ilāha illā Allāh, wa Allāhu akbar.” Therefore, tasbīḥ became better than recitation.

key_terms.أُسْرِيَ: was taken by night on the heavenly journey
key_terms.التَّسْبِيحُ: glorification of Allah by prescribed phrases
key_terms.الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the final two rakʿahs of a four-rakʿah prayer
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةَ: the angels praying behind the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.عَظَمَةِ اللَّهِ: the greatness and majesty of Allah

ai.seo_question: Why are some prayers recited aloud while Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr are recited quietly, and why is tasbīḥ preferred in the last two rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the reason for audible recitation in certain daily prayers and silent recitation in others by connecting these rulings to the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله heavenly ascent and the presence or absence of angels behind him. It also explains the preference of tasbīḥ in the last two rakʿahs as rooted in the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله glorification of Allah upon witnessing His عظَمة.
